serves.who: anyone turning the crank by hand (adult or child fingers, a few N of finger force)

arguments.why: The fused arc wall cannot work: short and thick it needs ~202 N (G6, user-confirmed fact) against a hand-force budget of 2-10 N, its root reaches 7.2%/6.1% strain against 1.38%/0.69% allowed, and the crank-peg sweep physically strikes any rim-riding finger once per turn (peg annulus r 5.9..11.1 covers the rim contact at r ~10.3, same z-range), which is the stall. A long thin fin floating 0.6 over the plate bends in-plane (no peel at a plate bond, root moment carried as in-plane stress at the pedestal), lands mid-window on force and under both strain limits; a doubly-fixed beam would need a 30 mm span that breaks the 10 mm bridge rule. The peg base is raised onto the flange top (invisible: same handle size, same top height) so its sweep passes 0.4 over the finger.

result.chosen: floating cantilever fin with reach finger (in-plane bending)
